table.caption: Fifteen questions to ask a blue Staffy breeder, and the answer to listen for
columns: What a good answer looks like
rows: Are both parents KC-registered?
The original KC registration certificates, shown to you, not photocopies.
Can I see the L-2-HGA and HC-HSF4 DNA test results?
Both parents clear, or carrier to clear — never carrier to carrier.
Can I see the mother with the puppies?
Yes. If the mother is not present, walk away: it is the single biggest puppy-farm signal.
How many litters does the dam have per year?
No more than four litters in her lifetime, as the registry recommends; more than two a year is a warning sign.
Have the puppies been vet-checked?
The name of the vet practice and the date of the check.
What vaccinations have they received?
At least the first vaccination before the puppy leaves at eight weeks.
Have they been microchipped?
Yes — UK law requires microchipping before sale.
What worming programme have they been on?
Wormed at two, five and eight weeks as a minimum.
Do you offer a health guarantee or purchase contract?
A written contract covering hereditary conditions.
Have the puppies been socialised with children, other dogs and household noise?
Yes, during the critical socialisation window of three to twelve weeks.
What food are they currently eating?
A feeding schedule, and a supply of the current food to take home.
Can I have references from previous buyers?
Contact details for past puppy families, offered without hesitation.
What happens if I can no longer keep the puppy?
The breeder takes the puppy back rather than let it go to a rescue.
Are you a member of the Staffordshire Bull Terrier Club?
Club membership, which shows a commitment to breed standards.
Can I visit the puppies more than once before deciding?
Yes. Any pressure to buy now or lose your spot is a manipulation tactic.

sections.heading: Socialisation, Training And The Vaccination Course
sections.intent: The three months that decide what kind of adult dog you have. Positive exposure to safe sights, sounds, people and vaccinated dogs; puppy classes; gentle handling so a vet visit is not a fight. Then the vaccination course, which starts at around eight weeks and covers distemper, parvovirus, leptospirosis and hepatitis: we give the first vaccination and the owner's own vet completes the course.
